text: Councilman and previous Mayor Michael Allawos has spent the last nine years on Glendora's City Council protecting and enhancing our small-town way of life and hometown values. As the representative for western Glendora's District 1, and the entire city, he has kept his promises by supporting Police and Fire with needed resources, expanding government transparency and communication, and standing with Glendora students and their parents.

Councilman Allawos has upheld strong Glendora development standards, preserved low-density planning, and supported local businesses and community development. He continues to communicate Glendora's needs to Sacramento and regional agencies, ensuring our voice is heard.

Working closely with city staff, Councilman Allawos has advanced improvements to roads, streetlights, and essential infrastructure. He remains committed to community-based public safety, addressing homelessness with outreach services, temporary shelter, and long-term strategies.
Financially, Glendora is stronger than ever, with record reserves and a triple AAA bond rating.

The next four years are too important to take risks with Glendora's future. Councilman Allawos brings a steady, calm hand and a proven problem-solving approach. He has kept his word to fight for our hometown values, always putting Glendora first, asking the hard questions, and always listening.

text: As a life-long Glendoran, community advocate and current candidate, I've heard the concerns of District 1. Fix our roads. Maintain the library and public places. Help with unaffordable, inequitable housing costs. Make sure all kids, families and residents are respected, protected and heard. Don't raise taxes.

Unfortunately, we all realize these can be competing concerns. To address them, we must talk, think, and work together. We must reject polarizing rhetoric that creates mistrust, pits neighbor against neighbor and distracts us from day-to-day life issues.

A quick internet search shows I have a proven track record bringing Glendora together. As a department chair and professor at Azusa Pacific University and a substitute teacher and aide in Glendora Unified, I've helped students and co-workers wrestle with difficult problems and controversies, while learning to better understand and appreciate various perspectives and solutions. As an office manager for a family-owned manufacturing company and a woman whose husband built a construction company from the ground up, I understand what it takes to ensure both working families and small businesses can thrive.
To elect someone experienced in building coalitions capable of responding to our shared community concerns, vote for me.
